public_rationale: Razeghi and colleagues' study, in the version available May 24, 2022, found substantial addition and multiplication performance gaps associated with pretraining frequency in the tested GPT-based models [e1]. This supports continuing difficulty with reliable arithmetic generalization in those models [e1]. The study also reports a simple task with a very small performance gap and discusses possible generalization, limiting any broader conclusion that the models cannot generalize at all [e1].
limitations: Frequency-associated performance gaps do not prove that models lack all abstraction ability or rely entirely on memorization [e1].
The findings concern the selected models and prompting conditions studied in 2022; they do not establish performance across all LLMs or in 2026 [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs doing arithmetic still have trouble with abstraction, even with new architectures and training regimes.

statement.excerpt: Same story; only the architectures and training regimes have changed. The troubles with abstraction persist.
statement.document_title: Happy Groundhog Day, The AI Edition

from_speaker: Yasaman Razeghi’s analysis of LLMs doing arithmetic
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that the arithmetic evaluations still reveal unreliable generalization across number cases despite newer architectures and training.
Only the architectures and training regimes have changed is read as rhetorical emphasis on persistence, not a literal denial of every other scientific change.
Training-frequency dependence is evidence of limited robustness; it is not proof that a model possesses no abstraction ability.
criteria.support_condition: The cited 2022 study finds material arithmetic-performance differences associated with the familiarity of numbers or their combinations in pretraining.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The cited study instead establishes robust arithmetic generalization across those cases without the alleged familiarity dependence.
